status: draft for semantic review before formal freeze
method: Manual consolidation of appended instructions only. The initial CUDA Agent skill and examples are preserved byte for byte. Source-bullet coverage does not by itself prove semantic equivalence.
scope: The additional instructions below apply to CUDA extension episodes in this workspace and do not relax the initial forbidden or allowed lists. Tool payload, transport, encoding and path issues are tool/workspace issues, not CUDA coding errors.

clauses.text: Use only the documented public allocation exception, preferably torch::empty_like in bindings. Do not replace a compiling binding with at::detail::empty_cuda, other at::detail::* symbols or private ATen APIs to bypass the dispatcher. For missing private allocation symbols, use the documented allocation path instead of guessed headers. Correctness and compilation take priority over allocation micro-optimizations; isolate any allocation optimization attempt and retain a known-good fallback.

On any compile failure, use the first actionable compiler error. Repair binding errors in binding files; missing allocation or binding symbols do not justify changing unrelated kernel math. Enforce float32, contiguous CUDA specialization with TORCH_CHECK or equivalent wrapper guarantees before interpreting storage as float*. For unreadable compile logs, use returned compiler output or rerun compile.

Finish edits and cleanup, then compile, verify, and profile or benchmark the exact submitted files. Do not finish after a write or submit an uncompiled final candidate. Any write after verification or benchmarking invalidates that evidence; earlier success does not excuse later failure. Preserve or restore the known-good version during post-benchmark optimization; if the new version fails, restore the known-good files and rerun compile, verification and benchmark. Cleanup also requires this final sequence.

Preserve model.py constructor and forward signatures; keep normal ModelNew.forward and nn.Module.__call__ hook behavior. Do not use __call__ = forward or another hook bypass unless explicitly required and revalidated; otherwise remove it before final validation. model_new.py may use allowed tensor creation and custom ops, not unsupported PyTorch computation to compensate for binding or kernel failures.

For workspace writes, supply operation: write, path and content as separate fields; do not omit operation or put Markdown/content in it. Unknown/missing operation, malformed payload, transport or encoding errors call for a clean tool retry; do not change CUDA kernel or binding logic solely in response to the tool failure. After any failed or ambiguous write, read the target before compiling: failure proves neither its contents nor that it stayed unchanged. Missing utility files or unreadable paths call for documented utilities or directory discovery, not conclusions about kernel correctness.

model_new.py configuration, arguments and forward path are part of correctness. After any kernel, binding or wrapper change, verify before using or reporting benchmark results; benchmark-only timing is a tuning probe. Finish edits/cleanup, compile if C++/CUDA/binding files changed, verify the exact final selection, then benchmark. Explicitly confirm unchanged compiled files and binary consistency when compilation is skipped. A compile followed by a write in the same step does not validate that later file; writes after verification stale it. Earlier/default verification does not validate a hardcoded config. On verification failure after tuning, reject the faster benchmark: fix the kernel/config and rerun compile, verification and benchmark, or restore the last verified version. Do not end after a benchmark-only edit; near the step limit preserve or restore the last fully validated version rather than make an unverified last-moment change.

Before hardcoding the fastest config, verify that exact selection across all verification shapes and seeds. Shape-specialized and non-default paths need correct fallbacks or must be unreachable; a fast path wrong for a harness shape must not remain selected. No diagnostic, debug, no-op or copy-only config may remain reachable from the final model path. Remove or disable unused configs unless all retained configs are semantically correct on supported shapes. On a config-specific failure, first inspect dispatch guards, F/N assumptions and fallback coverage; do not alter unrelated kernel math or move the failure into Python.

Before final validation remove intermediate kernel versions, unused tuning branches and diagnostic no-op/copy kernels from kernels/, except support required by the final default path. Do not submit diagnostic configs producing no output or merely copying, even if useful during tuning. Verify and benchmark the exact cleaned files.
Warnings such as Failed to find real location of python.exe alongside explicit compile success are not compiler errors or CUDA bugs. Use the explicit status and actionable compiler/runtime output.
For an unreadable compile log, use returned compiler output or rerun compile; a log-path failure does not justify unrelated kernel changes.

Do not continue tuning model_new.py configs while the underlying kernel is failing verification; restore correctness first. If a rewrite breaks it, use the last passing kernel as the baseline, prefer a minimal fix over another broad rewrite, and keep a known-good copy until the replacement verifies.
After a failed or ambiguous workspace read as well as a write, read the target before compiling or further editing; a failed call establishes neither correct nor incorrect file contents.
The same environment-warning rule applies to explicit verification and benchmark success: failure-to-locate-python warnings do not override the returned tool status.

Temporary probes, alternate bindings, patch/debug files and launchers must not remain in the final module path; remove them from kernels/ or binding references. Keep temporary notes and patch files out of kernels/. After deleting a probe or reverting a binding, recompile to remove stale symbols, then verify and benchmark the cleaned files.

For FileNotFoundError or an unreadable compile, verification or profiling log, use returned tool output/status or rerun the relevant tool. A missing log establishes neither pass nor fail and does not justify changing kernel math, binding allocation or model_new.py based on the failed read alone.

Compile, verification and benchmark are separate gates: compilation alone validates neither math nor wrapper behavior, and probe timing proves no correctness. Do not end after a write, compile-only step or benchmark-only step following an edit, including a late config, dispatch or forward-path change. Recompile if native files changed, verify and benchmark the exact final files. A compile after verification leaves verification stale; recompile, verify and benchmark before completion. Timing from before a later edit is not final evidence. Preserve the last verified selection during probes; fix and revalidate or restore it if a new kernel, binding or wrapper fails, regardless of faster timing.

A config fast for one shape but unverified or incorrect for another harness case must not remain selected. No faster but unverified or known-wrong config, dispatch branch or wrapper path may remain reachable from the final model path.

When float2/float4 loads span the non-reduced axis, each lane is a distinct output column: retain separate accumulators, shared-memory partials and reciprocal normalization values through scaling and storing; do not sum lanes into one scalar or broadcast a shared scalar. If a vectorized reduction fails with most elements mismatched and the same wrong values across block shapes, inspect lane packing/reduction semantics first; do not automatically attribute this to a race or launch-config problem. Isolate scalar, vector copy/indexing and vector reduction paths in that order. Remove skip-reduction/copy diagnostics from the final path and, after fixing the vector path, verify both vector-eligible and non-vector fallback shapes.

Do not diagnose kernels by adding pow, mean, sqrt, other PyTorch reference calculations or debug tensor computation to ModelNew.forward/model_new.py. The verifier rejects PyTorch computation during candidate forward; that failure is an instrumentation violation, not evidence that the CUDA math is wrong. Compare references outside the submitted forward path and remove diagnostics before final validation.

Absolute candidate latency in this environment can change roughly twofold between runs as GPU clock state changes. Do not rank variants by absolute microseconds from separate runs: compare with torch.compile in the same benchmark invocation, or repeat/interleave measurements and report the candidate/baseline ratio; stability across clock states increases trust.

review_notes: P03 preserves the early unqualified compile instruction; P06 preserves the later compile-if-native-changed qualification. Their tension is retained, not silently resolved in the compression.
P03/P11 retain the known-good fallback guidance despite its tension with the initial skill's debug-the-optimized-version requirement.
P16 deliberately preserves the unverified clock-state causal claim. Removing it would change evidence quality as well as compression; it requires a separate correction condition.
Sources from future stages are coverage links only. A clause's stage is its earliest introduction; each generated stage must be reviewed for premature information before use.
